project_specification.project_name: Scholium — PostgreSQL-only backends and OpenAI-compatible LLM providers
project_specification.addition_summary: Make PostgreSQL and S3-API object storage the only supported backends for running Scholium: production refuses a SQLite database or filesystem storage, every other environment warns that SQLite is deprecated, the delivery files stop defaulting to SQLite, and developers get one command that starts the compose stack's PostgreSQL, MinIO and Mailpit for running the API on the host. In the same change, the AI pre-review pipeline gains an OpenAI-compatible provider and a configurable Anthropic base URL, so any endpoint speaking either protocol (DeepSeek in particular) can serve the reviews without vendor-specific code.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / FastAPI / SQLAlchemy 2.0 / PostgreSQL 16 or SQLite (apps/api, uv workspace) + Next.js App Router / TypeScript / Tailwind (apps/web, npm workspace); compose.yaml stack with PostgreSQL (pgvector pg16), MinIO, Mailpit, api, worker and web
existing_context.test_baseline: web measured 2026-11-18: 268 files, 5464 tests passed (npm test --workspace apps/web, on the Next 16 branch); API suite unmeasured in this session, run cd apps/api && uv run --all-packages pytest before relying on it
existing_context.conventions: Modules under apps/api/src/app/modules/<name> with colocated tests/ folders; settings read from env vars in app/settings.py and checked by Settings.validate_for_environment (production lists every problem in one RuntimeError); AI providers under app/modules/ai_review/providers implement LLMProvider and register in providers/__init__.py; HTTP clients are httpx and injectable for tests; pytest with xdist (-n 4); system tests in tests/e2e run the shipped programs (npm run test:system); npm only, root package.json holds scripts only

feature.description: System refuses SQLite and filesystem storage in production: with SCHOLIUM_ENV=production, Settings.validate_for_environment adds "DATABASE_URL must be a PostgreSQL URL in production (SQLite is deprecated)" when the scheme of DATABASE_URL is anything other than postgres, postgresql or postgresql+psycopg (sqlite:///, sqlite+pysqlite://, in-memory SQLite, mysql:// and the unset default sqlite:///./scholium.db all get it) and "STORAGE_BACKEND must be s3 in production" when STORAGE_BACKEND is fs, listed together with every other problem in the one Unsafe production configuration error; postgres://, postgresql:// and postgresql+psycopg:// URLs with STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 pass these two checks; dev and test environments still accept SQLite and fs; existing unit tests that build a passing production configuration set a PostgreSQL URL and S3 settings, and the system test that boots a complete production configuration uses the FakeS3 server that tests/e2e/conftest.py already provides through NodeFactory.s3() and the PostgreSQL named by TEST_DATABASE_URL, skipping with the reason "needs TEST_DATABASE_URL (PostgreSQL)" when it is unset

System warns that SQLite is deprecated outside production: the first time a process builds a SQLite engine, app/db.py writes one WARNING record to the log through the logger named "app.db" (the logging module, not warnings.warn) saying "SQLite is deprecated; use PostgreSQL and move existing data with python -m app.migrate_backend (see docs/deploy.md). SQLite remains only for tests and local development", the api and the worker build their engines through app/db.py and each log it at most once per process, and no warning is logged for a PostgreSQL engine; a module-level function in app/db.py resets the once-per-process flag so tests can start from a clean state; a test that captures the log sees exactly one WARNING record with that message after two SQLite engines are built, and none after a PostgreSQL engine is built

System stops defaulting to SQLite in its delivery files: the api image no longer sets DATABASE_URL (a container started without one gets the settings default sqlite:///./scholium.db, which stays the development default and which production refuses), .env.example shows the compose PostgreSQL URL postgresql+psycopg://scholium:scholium-local-only@db:5432/scholium as the example DATABASE_URL and says SQLite is deprecated, and a delivery-wiring test asserts that no ENV or ARG line of a Containerfile under deploy/containers and no uncommented KEY=value line of .env.example holds a sqlite URL (comments may still mention SQLite)

System starts only the backing services when a developer runs npm run stack:deps, which brings up the db, minio, minio-init and mailpit services of compose.yaml and leaves api, worker and web stopped; stack:up, stack:down, stack:logs, stack:reset, stack:deps and stack:smoke run their compose commands through scripts/stack-compose.sh, executed with the compose arguments (for example scripts/stack-compose.sh up -d --build), which picks the engine as today (STACK_COMPOSE, else podman-compose, else docker compose) and, whenever the chosen engine is podman-compose (auto-detected or named in STACK_COMPOSE), reads the first X.Y.Z from its --version output and refuses a podman-compose older than 1.6.0 with exit status 1 and a message naming the installed version, why (nested ${A:-${B}} defaults and COMPOSE_PROFILES in compose.yaml need 1.6.0) and the fix (pipx install podman-compose, or STACK_COMPOSE="docker compose"); a test runs the script against fake engine executables that print "podman-compose version 1.0.6" and "podman-compose version 1.6.0" and checks the exit status and the arguments passed through

System reads the LLM provider settings: AI_PROVIDER accepts fake, anthropic, openai and ollama, and any other value is refused in every environment by the same Settings check that refuses an unknown JOBS_MODE, with an error listing the accepted values; new string settings ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (empty string when unset, meaning the Anthropic SDK default), OPENAI_API_KEY (empty string when unset) and OPENAI_BASE_URL (default https://api.openai.com/v1, trailing slash removed) are read from the environment as Settings attributes of those names; production refuses AI_PROVIDER=openai without OPENAI_API_KEY, and refuses AI_PROVIDER=openai when the AI_HOSTED_MODEL environment variable is unset or empty, because its default is an Anthropic model id; no setting value of an API key appears in any error message

System generates AI pre-reviews through any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with AI_PROVIDER=openai: OpenAIProvider (name "openai", hosted, so unlisted drafts are refused before any request) takes model, base_url, api_key, client and sleep as optional constructor arguments that default to settings.AI_HOSTED_MODEL, settings.OPENAI_BASE_URL, settings.OPENAI_API_KEY, a lazily built client and time.sleep (so get_provider keeps calling it with no arguments), and POSTs to base_url + "/chat/completions" with Authorization: Bearer OPENAI_API_KEY, the AI_HOSTED_MODEL model, a system message holding the instructions and a user message holding the data blocks quoted as <data id="..."> exactly as the Ollama provider quotes them, max_tokens from the request, temperature 0 and stream false; it returns choices[0].message.content as the text (ignoring any reasoning_content) and the response's model as the model; a non-2xx answer that is not retried raises an error naming the provider and the HTTP status without the key; it retries a 429 or 5xx answer, a timeout or a dropped connection at most 2 more times (3 requests in total) with exponential backoff starting at 1 second, waiting the Retry-After value instead when the header holds a whole number of seconds (capped at 30 seconds; any other form falls back to the backoff), raises an error naming the provider and the exception class when a timeout or dropped connection outlasts the retries, and never retries any other 4xx; an answer with no choices, null or empty message content, or finish_reason "length" raises an error naming the provider and the reason instead of returning a partial review; the httpx client can be injected, otherwise one with a 120 second timeout is built on first use; tests use httpx.MockTransport and a fake sleep, and check the URL, headers, body, parsing, the unlisted refusal, each retry case with the number of requests made, and each rejected answer

System sends Anthropic-protocol requests to the endpoint named by ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: AnthropicProvider takes an optional base_url constructor argument defaulting to settings.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (get_provider keeps calling it with no arguments); when that is non-empty it builds its client with that base_url (for example https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic) and the same API key handling as today; when it is empty the client uses the SDK default exactly as before; a test checks the base URL the client is built with in both cases

System passes the provider settings through the stack: compose.yaml passes ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL to the api and worker with empty defaults, AI_PROVIDER keeps its fake default, and .env.example lists the three new settings with placeholders plus commented DeepSeek examples for both protocols (AI_PROVIDER=openai with OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com, and AI_PROVIDER=anthropic with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic), each with AI_HOSTED_MODEL set to a placeholder model id rather than a real one

System produces an AI pre-review through a running OpenAI-compatible server: a system test runs a stub HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 inside the test process that records each request and answers POST /v1/chat/completions with a fixed completion, starts the api with JOBS_MODE=thread, AI_PROVIDER=openai, OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<stub port>/v1, a test key and AI_HOSTED_MODEL=stub-model through the node environment, submits and lists a paper with the existing tests/e2e/e2e_harness.py helpers (a version becoming listed enqueues the ai_review job), and asserts that GET /v1/papers/{id}/ai-reviews returns a review naming provider openai and model stub-model and that the stub received the bearer key

System checks both providers against a real endpoint when a developer runs npm run test:llm-live, which runs the apps/api tests marked live_llm, which the default pytest run excludes (addopts becomes -m 'not slow and not live_llm'), and each test sends one listed request with one quoted data block through AnthropicProvider (base_url LLM_LIVE_BASE_URL as given) and through OpenAIProvider (base_url LLM_LIVE_OPENAI_BASE_URL, else LLM_LIVE_BASE_URL with /v1 appended) using LLM_LIVE_API_KEY and LLM_LIVE_MODEL passed as constructor arguments, asserting non-empty text, the echoed model, and that no thinking block or reasoning_content text reaches the returned text; every live_llm test is skipped with the reason "LLM_LIVE_BASE_URL, LLM_LIVE_API_KEY and LLM_LIVE_MODEL are not set" when any is missing; the variables are deliberately not the ANTHROPIC_* or OPENAI_* names, so injecting them never reroutes other tools; deploy/llm-live.env.tpl holds the 1Password references LLM_LIVE_BASE_URL=op://VAULT/ITEM/model-iq-base-url, LLM_LIVE_API_KEY=op://VAULT/ITEM/model-iq-key and LLM_LIVE_MODEL=deepseek-v4-1-flash for op run --env-file=deploy/llm-live.env.tpl -- npm run test:llm-live, and the key never appears in test output

System documents the supported backends and providers: docs/deploy.md marks SQLite deprecated (tests and local development only; a production start on SQLite or STORAGE_BACKEND=fs stops with the Unsafe production configuration error naming DATABASE_URL or STORAGE_BACKEND), shows moving an existing SQLite and fs node to PostgreSQL and S3 with python -m app.migrate_backend, shows host development against npm run stack:deps with the values for the ports compose.yaml publishes (DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://scholium:scholium-local-only@127.0.0.1:5433/scholium, STORAGE_BACKEND=s3, S3_ENDPOINT_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9000, S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=1, the MinIO user and password as S3 keys, SMTP_URL=smtp://127.0.0.1:1025), states the podman-compose 1.6.0 minimum, adds STORAGE_BACKEND=s3 and a PostgreSQL DATABASE_URL to the production checklist, and documents AI_PROVIDER=openai, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL with DeepSeek shown for both protocols and the model id left to the provider's documentation, and documents the opt-in npm run test:llm-live check run through op run with deploy/llm-live.env.tpl; docs/tech_architect.md names PostgreSQL and S3-API storage as the supported backends; the CLAUDE.md Stack section says PostgreSQL 16 with SQLite deprecated (tests only) and lists npm run stack:deps

System passes every suite after the change: npm test exits 0 with no containers running (SQLite stays the test database there), npm run test:pg exits 0 against PostgreSQL 16, and npm run test:system exits 0 with TEST_DATABASE_URL set, including the production-boot and OpenAI-compatible review tests; starting python -m app with SCHOLIUM_ENV=production and a sqlite DATABASE_URL exits non-zero naming DATABASE_URL, and with STORAGE_BACKEND=fs exits non-zero naming STORAGE_BACKEND, and starting it in dev on SQLite writes the "SQLite is deprecated" warning to its log once and serves /readyz with 200; this feature fixes in application code whatever stops these from holding, it does not re-implement features 1 to 9

project_specification.integration_points: app/settings.py: production validation gains the database and storage checks; AI_PROVIDER validation and the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL settings app/db.py: one deprecation warning per process when the engine is SQLite app/modules/ai_review/providers: new openai_provider.py registered in __init__.py; anthropic_provider.py honours ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL compose.yaml and .env.example pass and describe the new provider settings Root package.json gains the stack:deps script and routes the stack:* scripts through scripts/stack-compose.sh deploy/containers/api.Containerfile drops its sqlite DATABASE_URL default tests/e2e gains the OpenAI-compatible review test; the production-boot test moves to PostgreSQL and S3 Opt-in npm run test:llm-live (pytest marker live_llm) with 1Password references in deploy/llm-live.env.tpl, run through op run

constraints.constraint: npm test must keep passing with no containers, no network and no credentials: SQLite stays the database of npm test, the claw-forge gate and the Playwright journeys, and nothing in this spec makes those suites need PostgreSQL
Deprecation only: no SQLite code path (FTS5 search index, SQLite ledger triggers, dialect branches, app.migrate_backend's SQLite source) is removed or changed in behaviour

All existing tests must stay green; change a test only where it builds a production configuration that the new database or storage checks now refuse, and then give it a PostgreSQL URL and S3 settings rather than weakening the check
No new runtime dependency: the OpenAI-compatible provider uses httpx, already a dependency; do not add the openai SDK

Provider ids name protocols, not vendors: no DeepSeek-specific code, setting or model default anywhere under apps/; DeepSeek appears only in documentation, commented .env.example examples and the live-check template deploy/llm-live.env.tpl

Live LLM checks are opt-in only: no test in npm test, the claw-forge gate, test:pg or test:system calls a real LLM endpoint, and .env.tpl (which run.sh injects into claw-forge agents) gains no ANTHROPIC_*, OPENAI_* or LLM_LIVE_* entry
Every hosted provider keeps the listed-only guard of LLMProvider.complete: unlisted drafts are refused before any network request
API keys never appear in logs, error messages, review records or test output
Semantic search embeddings are out of scope: the hashing embedder stays the default and OLLAMA_URL keeps selecting Ollama embeddings; the new provider serves chat completions only
Never add dependencies to the root package.json (scripts only); use npm, never pnpm or yarn; compose files keep working with podman-compose 1.6.0 or later and with docker compose

project_specification.success_criteria: npm test is green with no containers running npm run test:pg is green against PostgreSQL 16 npm run test:system is green with TEST_DATABASE_URL set npm run stack:deps starts PostgreSQL, MinIO and Mailpit only, and the API runs on the host against them A production start on SQLite or filesystem storage is refused with the reason AI_PROVIDER=openai produces AI pre-reviews through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and AI_PROVIDER=anthropic honours ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL op run --env-file=deploy/llm-live.env.tpl -- npm run test:llm-live passes against the model-iq gateway on both protocols
